CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.claim: Istaġnā is an antonym of ittaqā and appears near taqwā in 96:7; in 80:5 the positive counterpart is piety in 80:9.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:8:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Das Verb wird hier offensichtlich als Antonym zu ittaqā (V. 5) gebraucht; auch in 96:7 steht istaġnā in der Nähe von taqwā

BURSEVI:v10p364/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p364/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p364/r11.claim: The person transgresses because he believes or sees himself as self-sufficient; the wording may describe Abu Jahl and his companions or Pharaoh's claim to divinity.
BURSEVI:v10p364/r11.anchor: مفعول له أي يطغى لأن رأى وعلم نفسه مستغنيا أو أبصر مثل أبي جهل

QASHANI:96:3-8/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:3-8/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:3-8/r3.claim: God taught the Prophet what he had not known and granted knowledge so that, before he was firmly established in abiding, he would not claim independent perfection and transgress through selfhood; self-sufficiency produces transgression.
QASHANI:96:3-8/r3.anchor: لم يكن له علم فعلمه بعلمه ووهب له صفة عالميته لئلا يرى ذاته موصوفة بصفة الكمال فيطغى

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r9.claim: A person transgresses when he sees himself as self-sufficient and becomes blind to his need; if he witnesses his need rather than admiring himself, he does not transgress.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r9.anchor: فإذا لم يكن معجبا بنفسه ، وكان مشاهدا لمحل افتقاره - لم يكن طاغيا

SULAMI:v2p407#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r1.claim: Seeing oneself as wealthy breeds tyranny and arrogance through pride.
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : رؤية الغنى تورث الطغيان والبطر ، لأنه يورث الفخر

SULAMI:v2p407#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r2.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r2.claim: Knowledge and wealth each produce tyranny; asceticism protects from tyranny in worship, and persistent hunger helps reach asceticism by cutting desire for sin.
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r2.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ : في الدنيا طغيانان : طغيان العلم ، وطغيان المال

SULAMI:v2p407#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r3.claim: Wealth harms one whose proper state is poverty; feeling self-sufficient through wealth makes him insolent toward the Enricher.
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : طغيان الغني لمن لا يصلح له إلا الفقر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says two people are insatiable—the scholar and the worldly person; they differ because the scholar gains God's approval while the worldly person persists in transgression, linking these verses with the verse about learned fear.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : منهومان لا يشبعان : صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا ، ولا يستويان ، فاما صاحب العلم فيزداد رضا الرحمن

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra recounts Abu Jahl threatening to trample Muhammad while he prayed, then retreating when he saw a fiery trench and angels; the Prophet says angels would have seized him, and the narrator is unsure whether the verse was named in the report.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي حازم ، عن أبي هريرة قال : قال أبو جهل : هل يعفى محمد وجهه بين اظهركم ؟ قالوا : نعم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r2.speaker: عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r2.claim: Abdullah repeats that the scholar and worldly seeker are both insatiable but unequal, reciting the verses about transgression and learned fear.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r2.anchor: عن عون قال : قال عبد الله : منهومان لا يشبعان ، صاحب العلم وصاحب الدنيا ، ولا يستويان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r7.claim: Kalla is a rebuke and invalidation; appearing before any obvious target indicates that the intended target follows, namely the one who forbids a servant from praying.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r1.claim: Kalla normally follows the speech it rejects, but here it opens the sentence because the following statement is what deserves repudiation; Imru al-Qays offers a similar initial negative particle.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r1.anchor: وحق { كلا } أن تقع بعد كلام لإبطاله والزجر عن مضمونه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r4.claim: The accounts can be reconciled: the passage beginning at 96:9 directly concerns Abu Jahl, while the statement about human transgression through 96:8 prepares for it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r4.anchor: ووجه الجمع بين الروايتين : أن النازل في أبي جهل بعضه مقصود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r5.claim: Exegetes disagree whether these verses followed the first five immediately; prayer's mention seems problematic if obligatory prayer began at the Night Journey years later. Some posit intervening revelation and later attachment, while others deny this was the first revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r5.anchor: واختلفوا في أن هذه الآيات إلى آخر السورة نزلت عقب الخمس الآيات الماضية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r11.claim: The pronoun in raʾāhu refers to the human, seeing himself as rich; this is inward perception close to knowledge, which permits the reflexive-object construction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r11.anchor: والضمير في رآه للإنسان المذكور، كأنه قال: أن رأى نفسه غنيا، وهي رؤية قلب تقرب من العلم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r12.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r12.claim: Most readers lengthen the vowel in an raʾāhu; they differ on imala and its absence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r12.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «أن رآه» ، بالمد على وزن رعاه، واختلفوا في الإمالة وتركها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r13.speaker: ابن كثير من طريق قنبل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r13.claim: Ibn Kathir through Qunbul reads raʾahu short, deleting the weak final letter for ease.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r13.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير من طريق قنبل: «أن رأه» ، على وزن رعه، على حذف لام الفعل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#5/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#5/r1.claim: To see himself as self-sufficient means that he sees himself as having no need of anyone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#5/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي أن رأى نفسه استغنى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r1.claim: A person becomes exultant and transgressive upon seeing himself wealthy; he returns to God, who will question how wealth was acquired and spent.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن الإنسان أنه ذو فرح وأشر وبطر وطغيان، إذا رأى نفسه قد استغنى وكثر ماله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r2.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says that the knowledge-seeker and worldly seeker are insatiable, but the former grows in the Merciful's approval while the latter persists in transgression; he recited 35:28.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r2.anchor: عن عون قال: قال عبد الله: منهومان لا يشبعان، صاحب العلم وصاحب الدنيا، ولا يستويان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r3.claim: A version raised to the Prophet says that the knowledge-seeker and worldly seeker are two insatiable people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r3.anchor: وقد روي هذا مرفوعا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "منهومان لا يشبعان: طالب علم، وطالب دنيا"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl swearing to trample Muhammad while he prayed; as he approached he recoiled, describing a trench of fire, terror, and wings. The Prophet says angels would have snatched him limb by limb; the narrator is unsure whether the revelation context was part of Abu Hurayra's report. Ibn Kathir says Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmit it through Mu'tamir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم؟ قالوا: نعم. قال: فقال: واللات والعزى لئن رأيته يصلي

FARRA:v3p278/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p278/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p278/r3.claim: The self pronoun is omitted in “when he saw himself self-sufficient”: Arabic supplies it with reflexive actions, and can drop it when the verb has a predicate.
FARRA:v3p278/r3.anchor: ولم يقل: أن رأى نفسه والعرب إذا أوقعت فلا يكتفي باسم واحد على أنفسها،

FARRA:v3p278/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p278/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p278/r4.claim: Arabic says “when do you see yourself going out?” or “when do you think yourself going out?” with nafs omitted before a predicate.
FARRA:v3p278/r4.anchor: فإذا كان الفعل يريد: اسما وخبرا طرحوا النفس فقالوا: متى تراك خارجا، ومتى تظنك خارجا؟

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#2/r1.claim: A human being transgresses when he sees himself as self-sufficient.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#2/r1.anchor: {إن الإنسان ليطغى * أن رآه استغنى} أي يطغى أن رأى نفسه استغنى.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and has seventeen verses.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads رئيه with fatḥa on rāʾ and kasra on hamza; other readings differ in these vowels and in whether an alif follows hamza.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r4.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو: رئيه بفتح الراء وكسره الهمزة،

KASHSHAF:96:7/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:7/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:7/r1.claim: Raʾahu means he saw himself, with saw and knew among heart verbs taking two pronouns; it means knowing rather than sight because sight would not take both pronouns.
KASHSHAF:96:7/r1.anchor: أن رأى نفسه .   يقال : في أفعال القلوب

KASHSHAF:96:7/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:7/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:7/r2.claim: Istaghna is the second object of the verb.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r6.claim: The person imagines himself independent of his Lord.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r6.anchor: استغنى } أي عن ربه , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r7.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r7.claim: Alternatively, he considers himself self-sufficient through money and wealth; al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed about Abu Jahl.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r7.anchor: ويحتمل ثانيا : استغنى بماله وثروته , وقال الكلبي : نزلت في أبي جهل .

NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#2/r1.claim: “He sees himself” means he knows himself to be self-sufficient; the mental verb can take the two pronouns together, unlike physical seeing.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#2/r1.anchor: أن رأى نفسه يقال فى أفعال القلوب رأيتنى وعلمتنى ومعنى الرؤية العلم

NAHHAS:v5p261/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r12.claim: The object pronoun is attached directly to raʾā; raʾā belongs to the verbs that take a second predicative object like ẓanna.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r12.anchor: رأى نفسه لأنه من أخوات ظننت

QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r1.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r1.claim: One report says the passage was revealed about Abu Jahl; another says the entire sura came when he barred the Prophet from prayer, which would make it later than the first revelations.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى } إلى آخر السورة. قيل: إنه نزل في أبي جهل.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r2.claim: The first five verses may have come first and the remainder later about Abu Jahl, with God ordering their placement together, just as the last-revealed al-Baqara 2:281 was joined to much earlier verses.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون خمس آيات من أولها أول ما نزلت، ثم نزلت البقية في شأن أبي جهل،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Abu Salih, recounts that Abu Jahl demanded Meccan mountains of gold so he could become wealthy, transgress, and then abandon his faith; Gabriel offered that God could grant it but punish them like the table community, and the Prophet declined to spare them.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية أبي صالح عنه، قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes seeing oneself as having wealth to mean having a tribe, supporters, and helpers.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r5.anchor: وقيل: «أن رآه استغنى» بالعشيرة والأنصار والأعوان.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r6.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r6.claim: Al-Farra explains the omitted causal lām and says ra'a takes a subject and predicate like verbs of supposing, so Arabic need not state the reflexive self; he cites forms such as I saw myself and when do you think yourself to be leaving.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء: لم يقل رأى نفسه، كما قيل قتل نفسه لأن رأى من الأفعال التي تريد اسما وخبرا،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r7.speaker: مجاهد وحميد وقنبل عن ابن كثير
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r7.claim: Mujahid, Humayd, and Qunbul from Ibn Kathir read ra'ahu with a shortened hamza; the other readers lengthen it, which is preferred.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r7.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد وقنبل عن ابن كثير «أن رأه استغنى» بقصر الهمزة.

QUTB-ZILAL:96:6/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:6/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:6/r2.claim: God is also the source who gave the transgressor wealth, as well as his creation, honor, and knowledge.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:6/r2.anchor: كما أنه هو الذي خلقه وأكرمه وعلمه

QUTB-ZILAL:96:7/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:7/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:7/r1.claim: Humanity generally, except those whom faith protects, fails to thank God when enriched or recognize Him as the source of its gifts, then transgresses.

QUTB-ZILAL:96:7/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:7/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:7/r2.claim: Wealth should prompt recognition and gratitude, whereas people instead become rebellious, excessive, boastful, and arrogant.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:7/r2.anchor: من حيث كان ينبغي أن يعرف ثم يشكر

RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r1.speaker: الأخفش
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash parses the clause as ‘because he saw him,’ with the lām of li-anna deleted.
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r1.anchor: قال الأخفش : لأن رآه فخذف اللام

RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r2.claim: Al-Farra explains the omission of ‘himself’: raʾā governs a noun and predicate like verbs of supposition, and Arabic omits nafs with this verb class.
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r2.anchor: قال الفراء إنما قال : { أن رءاه } ولم يقل : رأى نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r3.claim: One reading of istaghna is that the human considers wealth sufficient without his Lord, but this cannot explain everyone: Solomon and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf remained humble when wealthy.

RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r4.claim: The commentator rejects treating wealth itself as necessarily producing arrogance: a rational person sees greater dependence on God when rich, since he must preserve himself, wealth, and dependents.
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r4.anchor: العاقل يعلم أنه عند الغنى يكون أكثر حاجة إلى الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r5.claim: The sīn in istaghna can mark seeking: a person imagines his effort earned wealth rather than God's gift and enabling; many who strive die hungry, and the wealthy will learn their riches were not their own achievement.
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r5.anchor: وفي الآية وجه ثالث : وهو أن سين { استغنى } سين الطالب

RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r6.claim: The surah opens by praising knowledge and ends by condemning wealth, thereby urging religion and learning and turning people away from worldly wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v32p19#3/r6.anchor: أول السورة يدل على مدح العلم وآخرها على مذمة المال

SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r1.claim: An raʾāhu is purposive: because a person sees himself as self-sufficient; this verb pattern may take two attached pronouns.
SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r1.anchor: أن " مفعول له، أي: لرؤيته نفسه مستغنيا. وتعدى الفعل هنا إلى ضميريه المتصلين

SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says seeing here means knowing, since visual raʾā cannot combine two pronouns; istaghnā is the second object.
SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r2.anchor: ومعنى الرؤية العلم لو كانت بمعنى الإبصار لامتنع في فعلها الجمع بين الضميرين

SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r3.claim: Some grammarians say visual raʾā can take the construction of cognitive raʾā; ʿĀʾisha's report and a verse about being a target of spears are offered as evidence.
SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r3.anchor: ذهب جماعة إلى أن " رأى " البصرية تعطي حكم العلمية، وجعل من ذلك قول عائشة - رضي الله عنها

SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r4.speaker: قنبل
SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r4.claim: Qunbul is reported with a reading omitting the alif in raʾāhu, a rare contraction; the author says a transmitted reading with a plausible basis should not be called an error, contra Ibn Mujāhid.
SAMIN-DURR:96:7/r4.anchor: ولا ينبغي ذلك لأنه إذا ثبتت قراءة ولها وجه وإن كان غيره أشهر منه فلا ينبغي أن يقدم على تغليطه

STUDYQURAN:96:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r3.claim: Self-sufficiency conveys a negative claim to independence from God and is the root of rebelliousness.
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r3.anchor: Beyond need is literally “self-sufficient,” but beyond need better conveys the negative connotation

TAB:96:6/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:6/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:6/r1.claim: It is wrong for a person to receive God's gifts of sound creation, knowledge, and unmatched favor, then disbelieve and transgress against Him.
TAB:96:6/r1.anchor: ما هكذا ينبغي أن يكون الإنسان أن يُنْعِمَ عليه ربّه بتسويته خَلقه ،   وتعليمه ما لم يكن يعلم

TAB:96:6/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:6/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:6/r2.claim: The human oversteps bounds, grows arrogant toward God, and disbelieves because he sees himself as self-sufficient.
TAB:96:6/r2.anchor: إنّ الإنْسانَ لَيَطْغَى أنْ رآهُ اسْتَغْنَى ،   يقول :  إن الإنسان ليتجاوز حدّه

TAB:96:6/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:6/r3.speaker: author
TAB:96:6/r3.claim: In grammar, raʾā takes a subject and predicate, so Arabs use a self-referential pronoun plus a second complement; verbs taking one object instead take an explicit reflexive noun.
TAB:96:6/r3.anchor: أنْ رآهُ اسْتَغْنَى لحاجة «رأى » إلى اسم وخبر ،   وكذلك تفعل العرب في كل فعل اقتضى الاسمَ والفعلَ

TAB-FULL:v24p533/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p533/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p533/r1.claim: Humans transgress and grow arrogant toward God, disbelieving when they see themselves as self-sufficient; Ṭabarī also explains Arabic reflexive phrasing for seeing oneself.
TAB-FULL:v24p533/r1.anchor: مكنيا عنها فيقول: متى تراك خارجا؟ ومتى تحسبك سائرا؟

TAB-FULL:v24p533/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p533/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p533/r2.claim: The verb raʾā here takes a subject and predicate, so Arabs use a reflexive pronoun when the speaker makes the self the object; a verb taking only one object instead uses nafsaka.
TAB-FULL:v24p533/r2.anchor: فإذا كان الفعل لا يقتضي إلا منصوبا واحدا، جعلوا موضع المكنى نفسه، فقالوا: قتلت نفسك، ولم يقولوا: قتلتك ولا قتلته

TABATABAI:96:7-14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:7-14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:7-14/r2.claim: Raʾā here means mental judgment, not visual sight; the human is both subject and object, and the clause explains why he transgresses: he supposes himself independent.
TABATABAI:96:7-14/r2.anchor: وجملة { أن رآه استغنى } في مقام التعليل

TABATABAI:96:7-14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:7-14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:7-14/r3.claim: The self-sufficient person attends to himself and outward means, forgets the Lord who blessed him, and then transgresses.
TABATABAI:96:7-14/r3.anchor: فيغفل عن ربه من غير أن يرى حاجة منه إليه

ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r3.claim: These verses were revealed concerning Abū Jahl ibn Hishām, who threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying.
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r3.anchor:
هذه نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام، وكذلك: (أرأيت الذي ينهى (9) عبدا إذا صلى (10).
لأن أبا جهل قال: إن رأيت محمدا يصلي توطأت عنقه.

TABRISI:96:2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2/r11.claim: Grammatically, the hidden subject of ra'ahu returns to the hidden subject of yatgha, and its object pronoun also refers to that subject; this is allowed with verbs of knowing because their predicate is the subject itself, unlike ordinary verbs that need nafsi.
TABRISI:96:2/r11.anchor: الضمير المستكن في رآه عائد إلى الضمير المستكن في يطغى والهاء في رآه عائد إلى الضمير

TABRISI:96:2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2/r12.claim: The phrase ra'ahu istaghna is a second object of ra'ahu, with the implied sense that he sees himself self-sufficient.

TABRISI:96:3-10/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:3-10/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:3-10/r12.claim: A person transgresses because he sees himself independent of God through kin, wealth, or strength; it is the belief in self-sufficiency, not actual wealth, that produces tyranny.
TABRISI:96:3-10/r12.anchor: لأن رآه نفسه مستغنية عن ربه بعشيرته وأمواله وقوته

TABRISI:96:3-10/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:3-10/r13.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:96:3-10/r13.claim: When a man gained wealth, he expanded his clothes, mount, food, and drink; that was his transgression.
TABRISI:96:3-10/r13.anchor: كان إذا أصاب مالا زاد في ثيابه ومركبه وطعامه وشرابه فذلك طغيانه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171#2/r2.claim: “The human” is Abū Jahl; his transgression was that when wealthy he upgraded his clothes, mount, food, and drink. Al-Kalbī similarly describes him rising in status through dress and food.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171#2/r2.anchor: {إن الإنسان} يعني أبا جهل. [[ليطغى]] قال مقاتل: كلا إذا أصاب مالا زاد في ثيابه، ومركبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p172/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p172/r1.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p172/r1.claim: An raʾāhu means “because he saw him”; the lām of causation is omitted, as in the cited idiom.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p172/r1.anchor: قال الأخفش: معناه لأن رآه، فحذف اللام، كما يقال: إنكم لتطغون إن رأيتكم استغنيتم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p172/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p172/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p172/r2.claim: The verb raʾā ordinarily takes both an object and a predicate, like thought and supposition verbs; Arabic can omit the reflexive object, as in “I saw myself.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p172/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: ولم يقل رأى الإنسان، فقال قتل نفسه لأن رأى من الأفعال التي تريد اسما وخبرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p172/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p172/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p172/r3.claim: He sees himself as wealthy and so transgresses; God warns him of his return to Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p172/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: إن رأى نفسه غنيا، وكان موسرا فطغى فخوفه الله بالرجعة

WAHIDI-QT:96:7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:7/r1.claim: The person sees himself as self-sufficient.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r8.claim: The human transgresses when he sees himself as self-sufficient.

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r9.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r9.claim: Elmalılı says the later passage was revealed much later because of Abu Jahl; Bukhari and Tirmidhi relate Ibn Abbas's report that he threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying at the Kaaba.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r9.anchor: Ezcümle Buhârî ve Tirmizî’de İbn Abbas’tan rivayet edildiği üzere

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r10.claim: One interpretation takes the warning as addressed first to Abu Jahl, attached to the relative phrase, though this leaves the opening of the surah disconnected from it.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r10.anchor: bu surette رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى sûrenin evveline merbut olmamış, Ebû Cehil’in sözünü reddederek ona tevcîh-i hitab etmiş oluyor

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r11.claim: Others take kalla as affirmative “indeed” rather than rebuke, keeping the address directed to the Prophet.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r11.anchor: Onun için bazıları da burada “kellâ” zecr için değil

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r12.claim: Elmalılı prefers the Prophet as the initial addressee and takes kalla as a warning not to stop repeating the command to read, preserving the passage's coherence.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r12.anchor: nazmın insicâmı itibariyle de muvâfık olduğundan mâna şu olmak lâzım gelir

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r13.claim: The warning tells Muhammad not to stop reading: humans surely transgress when they see themselves as self-sufficient, as Abu Jahl exemplifies.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r13.anchor: çünkü insan muhakkak tuğyan eder azar, haddini aşar, hakka karşı gelir

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r14.claim: Seeing oneself as independent or already fulfilled causes transgression; return is ultimately to the Lord, from whom there is no escape, so no one should claim sufficiency or transgress.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r14.anchor: kendini artık ihtiyâcı yokmuş, gayeye ermiş, gınâ mertebesine gelmiş görmek, o re’y ü itikadda bulunmak sebebiyle azar

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r15.claim: Although the address is to the Prophet, the chief aim is to warn the self-sufficient transgressors, illustrated by the arrogant unbeliever who occasioned the revelation.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r15.anchor: Bununla beraber asıl murad istiğnâ ve tuğyan edenlere inzardır. Onun için sebeb-i nüzul olan müstağnî azgının tuğyânı bir misâl

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r1.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r1.claim: Most exegetes identify the criticized human as Abu Jahl; a report says he vowed to trample Muhammad while praying, but retreated when confronted by a fiery barrier and winged beings, and the Prophet said angels would have seized him; the event occasioned 96:6-19.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r1.anchor: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu 6. âyette eleştirilen “insan” ile bilhassa İslâm’ın en azılı düşmanlarından olan Ebû Cehil’in kastedildiğini belirtirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r2.claim: Beyond the occasion, the passage criticizes people in every age who forget God in life's struggle, rely only on themselves, and claim to need no divine help.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r2.anchor: hangi devirde olursa olsun insanın hayat mücadelesinde Allah’ı unutup yalnız kendine güvenmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r3.claim: Kallā is a negative particle indicating that what follows should not happen; here it rebukes arrogant ingratitude, self-sufficiency, and turning from truth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r3.anchor: kellâ kelimesi olumsuzluk edatı olup devamında kendisinden sonra anlatılanların aslında olmaması gerektiğini ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r4.claim: Humans are weak and depend on God and society; God owns and can remove all resources, so boasting, disobedience, superiority, and claiming control of one's fate reflect ignorance, weak faith, and lack of insight.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r4.anchor: İnsanların ellerinde bulunan bütün imkânların gerçek sahibi ise kendileri değil

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r1.claim: The particle an may be explanatory and causal, meaning because, as in 43:5.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Wird hier – wie z. B. auch in dem mittelmekkanischen Vers 43:5

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r2.claim: After verbs of perception, rāʾā takes an ordinary accusative suffix with reflexive meaning; al-Ṭabarī illustrates the usage with a parallel phrase.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Wie allgemein nach den verba sentiendi steht hier kein Reflexivpronomen, sondern ein einfaches Akkusativsuffix in reflexiver Bedeutung

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r3.claim: The early uses of istaġnā contrast implicitly with taqwā or fear of God, a central theme in late antique Christian monastic piety.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Alle drei frühmekkanischen Verwendungen des Verbs stehen in implizitem Gegensatz zu taqwā

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r4.claim: The author recommends translating istaġnā as considering oneself self-sufficient rather than behaving arrogantly: the self-sufficient person permits himself arrogance.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:7:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Die Übersetzung von istaġnā mit „an sich selbst genug haben“ anstelle von „selbstherrlich auftreten“ (so Paret) empfiehlt sich

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p388/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p388/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p388/r1.claim: The Quraysh reject guidance arrogantly because wealth makes them feel self-sufficient and indifferent to God; their stated objections disguise this real motive and their love of the world.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p388/r1.anchor: self-sufficient from God and their love for this world

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r1.speaker: ابن كثير فيما قرأت على قنبل
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr as read through Qunbul shortens رآه without the post-hamza alif; Aḥmad calls this mistaken and allows only the full form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير فيما قرأت على قنبل: أن رأه [7] قصرا بغير ألف بعد الهمزة في وزن: رعه.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r2.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r2.claim: These readers pronounce رآه with imāla of the rāʾ toward kasra and retain the alif after hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي: أن رآه بكسر الراء وبعد الهمزة ألف،

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r3.speaker: نافع وحفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r3.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ do not use imāla on the rāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r3.anchor: وقرأ نافع: أن رآه فتح، وحفص عن عاصم لا يكسرها أيضا،

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr opens the rāʾ and gives kasra to the hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r4.anchor: أبو عمرو يفتح الراء ويكسر الهمزة .

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r5.claim: The report of rāʾ with kasra means imāla of its fatḥa; some trusted readers also imale the rāʾ, hamza, and alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r5.anchor: قال أبو علي: ينبغي أن يعني بكسر الراء إمالة فتحتها نحو الكسرة،

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r6.claim: Deleting the long alif from a past-tense form cannot be inferred from rare deletions in an irregular imperfect; such deletion is not analogical.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r6.anchor: إن الحذف لا يقاس، لا سيما في نحو هذا إذا كان على غير قياس،

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r7.speaker: رؤبة
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r7.claim: Rūʾbah's poetic وصني witnesses an exceptional deletion in وصاني, too rare to license a general analogy.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r7.anchor: قال رؤبة : وصاني العجاج فيما وصني

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r8.claim: The poet's من را is not like Ibn Kathīr's reading: the poet metathesized hamza and then deleted after two consonants met, while the reading articulates hamza fully.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p423/r8.anchor: قيل: ليس الذي قرأه ابن كثير كذلك، وذاك أن الشاعر قلب الهمزة قلبا،

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p425/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p425/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p425/r1.claim: A poetic form أري عيني ما لم ترأياه preserves the hamza, then deletes it for the jussive and eases it as in المرأة and الكمأة.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p425/r1.anchor: والآخر: أن يكون حقق الهمزة كما حقق الآخر في قوله : أري عيني ما لم ترأياه فحذف للجزم، ثم خفف على حسب التخفيف في المرأة والكمأة.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p425/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p425/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p425/r2.claim: In أن رآه, أن introduces a subject-and-predicate clause, as shown by the attached pronoun; استغنى is its second object.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p425/r2.anchor: والدليل على ذلك اتصال الضمير في قول: أن رآه ولولا أنه الداخل على الابتداء، لم يجز اتصال الضمير

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p425/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p425/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p425/r3.claim: Imāla moves from the hamza to the preceding rāʾ as it does from an imaled alif; Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ leave it open, while Abū ʿAmr opens rāʾ but imales hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p425/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: قول ابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي: أن رآه أمالوا الفتحة التي على الراء لإمالة فتحة الهمزة،

IBNMUJAHID:v1p692/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p692/r1.speaker: ابن كثير عن قنبل
IBNMUJAHID:v1p692/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr as read by Qunbul omits the alif after hamza in رآه; Ibn Mujāhid calls this mistaken, since the word parallels رعاه with or without imāla.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p692/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير فيما قرأت على قنبل ﴿ أن رآه ﴾ بغير ألف بعد الهمزة وزن رعه

IBNMUJAHID:v1p692/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p692/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p692/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads رآه with fatḥa on rāʾ and kasra on hamza.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p692/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو / رءاه / بفتح الراء وكسر الهمزة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p692/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p692/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p692/r3.claim: These readers break rāʾ and lengthen an open hamza; Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read both relevant vowels open.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p692/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر وحمزة والكسائى / أن رءاه / بكسر الراء

QIRAAT-ER:96:7:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:96:7:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:96:7:2#1/r1.claim: The shortened-vowel form raʾahu contrasts with raʾāhu prosodically and does not change the root meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:96:7:2#1/r1.anchor: The difference is prosodic — shortened alif

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r8.claim: In an raahu istaghna, both attached pronouns refer to the human; raʾā is inward perception, which can take identical attached subject and object pronouns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r8.anchor: الفاعل ضمير الإنسان، وضمير المفعول عائد عليه أيضا، ورأى هنا من رؤية القلب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r9.claim: Most readers retain the alif in raʾāhu; a narration from Ibn Mujahid's transmitter deletes it, which Ibn Mujahid calls an impermissible error.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: أن رآه بألف بعد الهمزة، وهي لام الفعل وقيل: بخلاف عنه بحذف الألف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r10.claim: The author says the transmitted deletion should not be dismissed: Arabic has comparable non-analogical deletions, and authenticated readings must be accepted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r10.anchor: وينبغي أن لا يغلطه، بل يتطلب له وجها، وقد حذفت الألف في نحو من هذا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r11.speaker: العجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r11.claim: A line attributed to al-ʿAjjāj supplies an example of deleting the final alif in waṣṣānī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r11.anchor: قال: وصاني العجاج فيما وصني يريد: وصاني، فاحذف الألف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r12.claim: The deletion in the phrase law tarā ahl Makka is non-analogical, but transmitted readings are accepted whether regular or anomalous in Arabic usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r12.anchor: وقد حذفت في مضارع رأى في قولهم: أصاب الناس جهد ولو تر أهل مكة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r1.claim: The clause is causal: he transgresses because he sees himself as self-sufficient; rāʾā can govern a second object when it means to know, even with the same subject and object.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r1.anchor: مفعول من أجله أي يطغى لأن رأى نفسه مستغنيا على أن جملة استغنى مفعول ثان لرأى لأنه بمعنى علم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r2.speaker: جماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r2.claim: A group allows visual raʾā to take the same-subject construction of mental verbs; they cite ʿĀʾisha and a line by al-ʿAjjāj as evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r2.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى أن رأي البصرية قد تعطى حكم القلبية في ذلك وجعلوا منه قول عائشة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r3.claim: If raʾā is visual, the clause is circumstantial: arrogance follows merely from the appearance of wealth, without examining its reality.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r3.anchor: فإذا جعلت رأي هنا بصرية فالجملة في موضع الحال وتعليل طغيانه برؤيته لا بنفس الأستغناء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r4.claim: The two parses locate the cause either in his false belief that he is independent or in his unreflective sight of outward circumstances, as the warning in 42:27 suggests.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r4.anchor: مدار طغيانه زعمه الفاسد على الأول ومجرد رؤيته ظاهر الحال من غير رؤية وتأمل في حقيقته على الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r5.claim: The apparent meaning of self-sufficiency is financial wealth, though a reported alternative makes him think his clan, property, and strength free him from God.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r5.anchor: وعلى الوجهين المراد بالأستغناء الغني بالمال أعني مقابل الفقر المعروف وقيل المراد أن رأي نفسه مستغنيا عن ربه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r6.claim: A report says Abu Jahl asked the Prophet for Meccan mountains of gold and silver so the Quraysh might become rich, transgress, and then abandon their religion for his; Gabriel offered the request, but the Prophet refrained for their sake.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r6.anchor: أبا جهل قال لرسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أتزعم أن من استغنى طغى فاجعل لنا جبال مكة ذهبا وفضة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r7.speaker: قنبل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r7.claim: Qunbul, in one transmission, reads an-raʾahu without the alif after the hamza; Ibn Mujāhid calls the deletion impermissible, while al-Baḥr says a transmitted reading must be accepted and seeks its Arabic basis.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ قنبل بخلاف عنه أن رأه بحذف الألف التي بعد الهمزة وهي لام الفعل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r6.claim: The cause is that a person sees himself as self-sufficient.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r6.anchor: لأن {رآه استغنى} أن رأى نفسه غنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r7.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says the person rises in status through clothing, food, and similar comforts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r7.anchor: قال الكلبي: يرتفع عن منزلة إلى منزلة في اللباس والطعام وغيرهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r8.claim: Muqatil says the passage concerns Abu Jahl, who enlarged his clothing, mount, and food whenever he gained wealth; this was his transgression.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r8.anchor: وقال مقاتل: نزلت في أبي جهل، كان إذا أصاب مالا زاد في ثيابه ومركبه وطعامه

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r4.claim: كلا rebukes the one who rejects God's favor through transgression; a person transgresses when he sees himself as self-sufficient.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r4.anchor: كلا } ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله بطغيانه

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r5.claim: The clause means that a person sees himself and regards himself as independent; استغنى is the second object of رأى, meaning “know.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r5.anchor: أن رأى نفسه، واستغنى مفعوله الثاني لأنه بمعنى علم

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p24/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r4.claim: The warning turns to the human tendency to become arrogant about knowledge and status among created beings.
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r4.anchor: ويمضي البيان القرآني، في الردع المحذر مما يتعرض له الإنسان من غرور بعلمه ومكانه بين المحلوقات

BINTSHATI:v2p24/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r5.claim: طغيان means exceeding bounds, especially the tyranny of despots; استغناء is the opposite of need, and كلا rebukes and restrains.
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r5.anchor: الطغيان تجاوز الحد، وأكثر ما يستعمل في جبروت العتاة المستبدين. والاستغناء ضد الاحتياج

BINTSHATI:v2p25/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p25/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p25/r2.claim: The cause is not absorption in money or status; the text says the human imagines himself independent of his Creator and is lured by acquired knowledge into overstepping his place.
BINTSHATI:v2p25/r2.anchor: وليس الطغيان عن استغراق في حب المال والجاه كما تأوله بعض المفسرين

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.claim: Al-Razi’s second solution reads الإنسان generically: despite creation and blessings, people transgress, forget their return, and forbid worship when they should follow guidance and enjoin piety.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.anchor: أن تحمل الآيات على عموم لفظها في الظاهر، وهو أن الإنسان، جملة الإنسان، خلقه الله من علق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r9.claim: Seeing oneself as self-sufficient means inwardly recognizing one's own wealth; this is the dominant human tendency and changes conduct toward whatever one no longer needs.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r10.claim: A prophetic report says a human's belly is filled only by dust, underscoring that acquisitiveness has no natural endpoint.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r10.anchor: ولا يملأ جوف ابن آدم إلا التراب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r11.claim: A report about the last person to leave Hell says he swears not to ask for more, then requests further gifts after receiving what he sought, illustrating how satisfaction expands into further desire.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p482/r11.anchor: كما في حديث آخر أهل النار خروجا منها يقسم لربه أنه لا يسأل غير ما طلبه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r1.claim: When the Prophet foretold conquest and abundant meals, his hearers said the earlier days were better because they allowed more worship; he corrected them, saying their present state was better.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r1.anchor: أنتم اليوم خير من يومئذ , فقالوا : بل يومئذ , نتفرغ لعبادة ربنا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r2.claim: The Prophet said he feared prosperity and competition for worldly goods more than poverty, since such competition destroyed earlier peoples and could destroy his community.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p483/r2.anchor: ما الفقر أخشى عليكم , ولكن أخسى أن يبسط عليكم الدنيا كما بسطت

DURR:96:6/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:96:6/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says knowledge and worldly pursuit are both insatiable but unequal: knowledge brings divine approval, while pursuit of the world deepens transgression.
DURR:96:6/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : منهومان لا يشبعان : صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا

DURR:96:7/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:7/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:96:7/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says knowledge and worldly pursuit are both insatiable but unequal: knowledge brings divine approval, while pursuit of the world deepens transgression.
DURR:96:7/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : منهومان لا يشبعان : صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا

DURR:96:9/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:96:9/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says knowledge and worldly pursuit are both insatiable but unequal: knowledge brings divine approval, while pursuit of the world deepens transgression.
DURR:96:9/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : منهومان لا يشبعان : صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا

DURR:96:10/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:96:10/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says knowledge and worldly pursuit are both insatiable but unequal: knowledge brings divine approval, while pursuit of the world deepens transgression.
DURR:96:10/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : منهومان لا يشبعان : صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا

DURR:96:15/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:15/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:96:15/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says knowledge and worldly pursuit are both insatiable but unequal: knowledge brings divine approval, while pursuit of the world deepens transgression.
DURR:96:15/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : منهومان لا يشبعان : صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا

DURR:96:16/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:16/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:96:16/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says knowledge and worldly pursuit are both insatiable but unequal: knowledge brings divine approval, while pursuit of the world deepens transgression.
DURR:96:16/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : منهومان لا يشبعان : صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا

FARRA:v1p333/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p333/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p333/r1.claim: Arabic uses a direct reflexive expression with complete verbs (قتلتم أنفسكم; ظلموا أنفسهم), but defective cognition verbs take a pronoun attached to the verb (أظنني خارجا), distinguishing verbs that may be omitted from those that cannot.
FARRA:v1p333/r1.anchor: في الأفعال التامة غير ما يقولون في الناقصة

FARRA:v1p333/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p333/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p333/r2.claim: The Qurʾān says أن رآه استغنى rather than رأى نفسه; poetry can use a direct object with a complete verb, but forms such as عدمتني are not standard speech.
FARRA:v1p333/r2.anchor: أن رآه استغنى ولم يقل: رأى نفسه

TAB:96:7/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:7/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:7/r1.claim: ‘Kalla’ rebukes a human who receives God's gifts of sound creation, knowledge, and unmatched favors, then disbelieves and transgresses against Him upon seeing himself self-sufficient.
TAB:96:7/r1.anchor: ما هكذا ينبغي أن يكون الإنسان أن ينعم عليه ربه بتسويته خلقه

TAB:96:7/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:7/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:7/r2.claim: The human exceeds his limits and arrogantly disbelieves in his Lord because he sees himself as self-sufficient.
TAB:96:7/r2.anchor: إن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى

TAB:96:7/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:7/r3.speaker: author
TAB:96:7/r3.claim: The construction treats the reflexive pronoun as the subject and ‘self-sufficient’ as the predicate because raʾā needs both; Arabic uses similar forms with verbs like ‘consider,’ but a verb taking one object instead uses a reflexive object such as ‘you killed yourself.’
TAB:96:7/r3.anchor: أن رآه استغنى لحاجة «رأى » إلى اسم وخبر

BURHAN:v2p140/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p140/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p140/r5.claim: The Prophet's fear that worldly abundance and adornment will be opened to the community is associated with the human tendency to transgress when self-sufficient.
BURHAN:v2p140/r5.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فى مثل الدنيا إن مما أخاف عليكم ما يفتح عليكم من زهرة الدنيا وزينتها

ITQAN:v3p38/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p38/r8.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ITQAN:v3p38/r8.claim: Ibn al-Hajib says spouses precede children because spouses are more often enemies; wealth precedes children because it is more consistently a source of temptation and can lead a person to transgress.
ITQAN:v3p38/r8.anchor: إنما قدم الأزواج لأن المقصود الإخبار أن فيهم أعداء ووقوع ذلك في الأزواج أكثر منه في الأولاد

DAMGHANI:v1p49/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r5.claim: In the passage about transgression when one sees oneself as self-sufficient, al-insān refers to Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r5.anchor: الإنسان يعني أبا جهل بن هشام

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r4.claim: The human who transgresses after seeing himself as self-sufficient is identified as Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.

NASHR:v2p401/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p401/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p401/r4.claim: Most transmitters of Qunbul, including Ibn Mujāhid and Ibn Shanabūdh, report the short hamza without alif; al-Zaynabī alone reports Qunbul with lengthening.
NASHR:v2p401/r4.anchor: واختلف عن قنبل في أن رآه استغنى، فروى ابن مجاهد وابن شنبوذ، وأكثر الرواة عنه رأه بقصر الهمزة

NASHR:v2p401/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p401/r5.speaker: ابن مجاهد
NASHR:v2p401/r5.claim: Ibn Mujāhid judged Qunbul mistaken in the long form and may therefore have declined to transmit it; al-Khuzāʿī was said to have reported it from Qunbul's companions.
NASHR:v2p401/r5.anchor: إلا أن ابن مجاهد غلط قنبلا في ذلك، فربما لم يأخذ به، وزعم أن الخزاعي رواه

NASHR:v2p401/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p401/r6.speaker: الناس
NASHR:v2p401/r6.claim: Critics of Ibn Mujāhid argued that an established transmission must be followed despite weak Arabic support, and that al-Khuzāʿī's book does not mention this reading.
NASHR:v2p401/r6.anchor: ورد الناس على ابن مجاهد في ذلك بأن الرواية إذا ثبتت وجب الأخذ بها وإن كانت حجتها في العربية ضعيفة

NASHR:v2p401/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p401/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p401/r7.claim: The rebuttal is not binding: a transmitter who suspects an error need not report it except to clarify it, and a narrator's mistake does not make the underlying reading weak.
NASHR:v2p401/r7.anchor: ليس ما رد به على ابن مجاهد في هذا لازما فإن الراوي إذا ظن غلط المروي عنه

ABUHAYYAN:96:7/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:7/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:7/r1.claim: The subject and object pronouns in رآه both refer to the human; رأى is mental perception, which can take coreferential connected subject and object pronouns, unlike ordinary ضرب-type verbs.
ABUHAYYAN:96:7/r1.anchor: الفاعل ضمير الإنسان ، وضمير المفعول عائد عليه أيضاً ، ورأى هنا من رؤية القلب ، يجوز أن يتحد فيها الضميران متصلين

ABUHAYYAN:96:7/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:7/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:96:7/r2.claim: The majority read أن رآه with an alif after the hamza; a variant without that alif is transmitted by Ibn Mujahid from an unnamed reader.
ABUHAYYAN:96:7/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { أن رآه } بألف بعد الهمزة ، وهي لام الفعل ؛ وقيل : بخلاف عنه بحذف الألف ، وهي رواية ابن مجاهد عنه

ABUHAYYAN:96:7/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:7/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:7/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects calling the deletion an impossible error: Arabic sometimes deletes the root alif, as in al-ʿAjjaj's وصني and ولو تر أهل مكة, and an authenticated reading must be accepted, regular or non-regular.
ABUHAYYAN:96:7/r3.anchor: قال : وهو غلط لا يجوز ، وينبغي أن لا يغلطه ، بل يتطلب له وجهاً ، وقد حذفت الألف

ALUSI:96:7/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:7/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:7/r1.claim: The phrase gives the cause of transgression: he saw himself as self-sufficient; istaghnā is the second object of raʾā, used cognitively, allowing subject and object to share a referent.
ALUSI:96:7/r1.anchor: مفعول من أجله أي يطغى لأن رأى نفسه مستغنياً على أن جملة استغنى مفعول ثان لرأى لأنه بمعنى علم

ALUSI:96:7/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:7/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:7/r2.claim: Grammarians allow a single referent for subject and object with verbs of cognition and with faqada and ʿadima; this supports the cognitive reading of raʾā.
ALUSI:96:7/r2.anchor: ولذلك ساغ كون فاعله ومفعوله ضميري واحد نحو علمتني فقد قالوا إن ذلك لا يكون في غير أفعال القلوب وفقد وعدم

ALUSI:96:7/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:7/r3.speaker: جماعة
ALUSI:96:7/r3.claim: A group allows visual raʾā to take the same subject and object reference as cognitive verbs do.
ALUSI:96:7/r3.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى أن رأي البصرية قد تعطى حكم القلبية في ذلك

ALUSI:96:7/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:7/r4.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI:96:7/r4.claim: ʿĀʾisha’s wording, “I saw us with the Messenger of God with no food except the two blacks,” is cited as an example of visual raʾā; no grading is stated.
ALUSI:96:7/r4.anchor: وجعلوا منه قول عائشة لقد رأيتنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وما لنا طعام إلا الأسودان

ALUSI:96:7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:7/r5.speaker: قائل
ALUSI:96:7/r5.claim: A cited poetic line, “I see myself as a target for spears,” is offered in support of visual raʾā taking the same subject and object reference.

ALUSI:96:7/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:7/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:7/r6.claim: If raʾā is visual, istaghnā is a circumstantial clause; the apparent state he sees, rather than actual wealth, prompts his transgression, as 42:27 also indicates.
ALUSI:96:7/r6.anchor: فإذا جعلت رأي هنا بصرية فالجملة في موضع الحال وتعليل طغيانه برؤيته لا بنفس الاستغناء

ALUSI:96:7/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:7/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:7/r7.claim: On either grammatical analysis, self-sufficiency means financial wealth, the familiar opposite of poverty.
ALUSI:96:7/r7.anchor: وعلى الوجهين المراد بالاستغناء الغني بالمال أعني مقابل الفقر المعروف

ALUSI:96:7/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:7/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:7/r8.claim: Another, less apparent view says he sees himself independent of his Lord through his clan, wealth, and strength.
ALUSI:96:7/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد أن رأى نفسه مستغنياً عن ربه سبحانه بعشيرته وأمواله وقوته وهو خلاف الظاهر

ALUSI:96:7/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:7/r9.speaker: أبو جهل
ALUSI:96:7/r9.claim: A report says Abū Jahl challenged the Prophet to make Mecca’s mountains gold and silver so they could take it, transgress, leave their religion, and follow his; Gabriel offered this, warning of punishment like the people of the table if they disbelieved, but the Prophet refrained to spare them. No grading is given.
ALUSI:96:7/r9.anchor: ظاهر ما روى أن أبا جهل قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أتزعم أن من استغنى طغى فاجعل لنا جبال مكة ذهباً وفضة

ALUSI:96:7/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:7/r10.speaker: قنبل
ALUSI:96:7/r10.claim: Qunbul, in one transmission, reads an raʾā with the alif after the hamza omitted; Ibn Mujāhid calls the deletion impermissible and judges it an error.
ALUSI:96:7/r10.anchor: وقرأ قنبل بخلاف عنه أن رأه بحذف الألف التي بعد الهمزة

ALUSI:96:7/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:7/r11.speaker: البحر
ALUSI:96:7/r11.claim: Al-Baḥr says Ibn Mujāhid should seek a justification rather than censure Qunbul, since Arabic has comparable deletion of a root-final alif, including in cited usage and poetry.
ALUSI:96:7/r11.anchor: ينبغي أن لا يغلطه بل يتطلب له وجهاً

ALUSI:96:7/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:7/r12.speaker: البحر
ALUSI:96:7/r12.claim: Al-Baḥr notes that the deletion is irregular, but a soundly transmitted reading must be accepted: readings follow both regular and anomalous Arabic usage.
ALUSI:96:7/r12.anchor: وهو حذف لا ينقاس لكن إذا صحت الرواية وجب القبول فالقراآت جاءت على لغة العرب قياسها وشاذها

BAGHAWI:96:7/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:7/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:7/r2.anchor: رآه استغنى } أن رأى نفسه غنياً

BAGHAWI:96:7/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:7/r3.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI:96:7/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says the person rises from one level to another in clothing, food, and other comforts.
BAGHAWI:96:7/r3.anchor: قال الكلبي : يرتفع عن منزلة إلى منزلة في اللباس والطعام وغيرهما

BAGHAWI:96:7/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:7/r4.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI:96:7/r4.claim: Muqatil says the verse was revealed about Abu Jahl, who, when he gained money, increased his clothes, mount, and food; that was his transgression.
BAGHAWI:96:7/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل : نزلت في أبي جهل ، كان إذا أصاب مالاً زاد في ثيابه ومركبه وطعامه ، فذلك طغيانه

BAYDAWI:96:7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:7/r1.claim: The person sees himself as self-sufficient; istaghnā is the second object of raʾā, which here means “know,” allowing subject and object to be the same pronoun.
BAYDAWI:96:7/r1.anchor: واستغنى مفعوله الثاني ؛ لأنه بمعنى علم

BIQAI:96:7/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:7/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:7/r1.claim: The particle an gives the cause: the human transgresses because he sees himself as self-sufficient; the emphasis responds to widespread denial, since no tyrant admits transgression.

BIQAI:96:7/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:7/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:7/r2.claim: Raʾāhu means that a person knows his own condition through immediate, inward awareness.

BIQAI:96:7/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:7/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:7/r3.claim: Once people feel independent of something, they become blind to their need for it, change their conduct, and exceed proper limits; no son of Adam is filled except by dust.
BIQAI:96:7/r3.anchor: ولا يملأ جوف ابن آدم إلا التراب

BIQAI:96:7/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:7/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:7/r4.claim: A report about the last person to leave the Fire says he keeps asking for more: after each request is granted and he feels satisfied, he asks for something else until admitted to the final abode.
BIQAI:96:7/r4.anchor: حديث آخر أهل النار خروجاً منها

BIQAI:96:7/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:7/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:7/r5.claim: Biqāʿī warns that the needy Muslim community will receive the earth's treasures and become tyrannical through wealth, as earlier communities did, though its members deny this danger.
BIQAI:96:7/r5.anchor: ستفتح لها خزائن الأرض فيطغيها الغنى

BIQAI:96:7/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:7/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:96:7/r6.claim: The Prophet warned that when the community is served abundant food morning and evening, people will compete for worldly wealth and be destroyed as earlier peoples were; he said they are better off in their present poverty.
BIQAI:96:7/r6.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم حين بشرهم بالفتوحات

IBNASHUR:96:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:7/r1.claim: Istiġnā means intense wealth or self-sufficiency; the added sīn and tāʾ intensify the action, as in istajāba and istaqarra.
IBNASHUR:96:7/r1.anchor: والاستغناء :  شدة الغنى ،  فالسين والتاء فيه للمبالغة في حصول الفعل مثل استجاب واستقر .

IBNASHUR:96:7/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:7/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:7/r2.claim: The clause an raʾāhu is attached to yaṭghā with a deleted causal lām: a person transgresses because he sees himself self-sufficient.
IBNASHUR:96:7/r2.anchor: و { وَأنْ رآه } متعلق ب« يطغى » بحذف لام التعليل لأن حذف الجار مع ( أنْ ) كثير شائع

IBNASHUR:96:7/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:7/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:7/r3.claim: The felt independence makes the wealthy person think he needs no one and that others need him; without religious or rational restraint, this grows into contempt and abuse, since he feels protected by weapons, servants, allies, and beneficiaries of his wealth.
IBNASHUR:96:7/r3.anchor: وعلة هذا الخلق أن الاستغناء تحدث صاحبه نفسه بأنه غير محتاج إلى غيره وأن غيره محتاج فيرى نفسه أعظم من أهل الحاجة

IBNASHUR:96:7/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:7/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:7/r4.claim: The verse exposes a major psychological truth about character and warns against allowing this sense of self-sufficiency to take root.
IBNASHUR:96:7/r4.anchor: فقد بينت هذه الآية حقيقةً نفسية عظيمة من الأخلاق وعلم النفس .  ونبهت على الحذر من تغلغلها في النفس .

IBNASHUR:96:7/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:7/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:7/r5.claim: Both the subject pronoun and object pronoun in raʾāhu refer to the human: he sees himself as self-sufficient; shared subject and object are allowed with verbs of supposition such as ẓanna and its sisters.
IBNASHUR:96:7/r5.anchor: وضمير { رآه } المستتر المرفوع على الفاعلية وضميرُه البارز المنصوب على المفعولية كلاهما عائد إلى الإنسان ،  أي أن رأى نفسه

IBNASHUR:96:7/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:7/r6.speaker: الفراء
IBNASHUR:96:7/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Arabic commonly drops nafs in this class of supposition verbs, yielding expressions such as raʾaytuni and ḥasib tuni.
IBNASHUR:96:7/r6.anchor: قال الفراء :  والعرب تطرح النفس من هذا الجنس ( أي جنس أفعال الظن والحسبان ) تقول :  رأيتني وحسبتني

IBNASHUR:96:7/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:7/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:7/r7.claim: Many grammarians extend the mental raʾā construction to visual raʾā; Qaṭarī ibn al-Fujāʾa's verse, with the speaker seeing himself a target for spears, illustrates it.
IBNASHUR:96:7/r7.anchor: وألحقت ( رأى ) البصرية ب ( رأى ) القلبية عند كثير من النحاة كما في قول قطري بن الفجاءة :  فلقد أراني للرماح دريئة

IBNASHUR:96:7/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:7/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:7/r8.claim: A rare poetic parallel by al-Nimr ibn Tawlab uses a reflexive object with a visual verb; faqd and ʿadim also take this form in supplications such as faqadtuni and ʿadimtuni.
IBNASHUR:96:7/r8.anchor: ومن النادر قول النّمر بن تَوْلَب :  قد بِتُّ أَحْرُسُنِي وَحْدِي وَيَمْنَعُنِي

IBNASHUR:96:7/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:7/r9.speaker: ابن مجاهد عن قنبل
IBNASHUR:96:7/r9.claim: All readers use the form with an alif after the hamza; Ibn Mujāhid alone reports that Qunbul, from Ibn Kathīr, read it without that alif.
IBNASHUR:96:7/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجميع أن رآه } بألف بعد الهمزة ،  وروى ابن مجاهد عن قنبل أنه قرأه عن ابن كثير « رأه » بدون ألف

IBNASHUR:96:7/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:7/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:7/r10.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects Ibn Mujāhid's dismissal of the variant as an error because he explicitly attributes it to Qunbul, while noting that no one else reports this anomalous reading.
IBNASHUR:96:7/r10.anchor: قال ابن مجاهد :  هذا غلط ولا يعبأ بكلام ابن مجاهد بعد أن جزم بأنه رواه عن قنبل ،  لكن هذا لم يروه غير ابن مجاهد

IBNATIYYA:96:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r1.claim: Wealth leads a person to tyranny unless God protects him.
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r1.anchor: والغنى : مطغ إلا من عصم الله

IBNATIYYA:96:7/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r2.claim: The pronoun in raʾāhu refers to the previously mentioned human: he sees himself as wealthy.

IBNATIYYA:96:7/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r3.claim: This is an inward, near-to-knowing perception, so the verb may act reflexively, as in I found myself or thought myself, unlike I struck myself.
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r3.anchor: وهي رؤية قلب تقرب من العلم ، ولذلك جاز أن يعمل فعل الفاعل في نفسه

IBNATIYYA:96:7/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r4.claim: The majority read raʾāhu with a long vowel; they differed over imāla.
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : «أن رآه » بالمد على وزن رعاه ، واختلفوا في الإمالة وتركها

IBNATIYYA:96:7/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r5.speaker: ابن كثير من طريق قنبل
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir through Qunbul reads raʾahu without the long vowel, deleting the verb’s final radical for lightening.
IBNATIYYA:96:7/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير من طريق قنبل : «أن رأه » ، على وزن رعه ، على حذف لام الفعل وذلك تخفيف

IBNKATHIR:96:6/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:6/r1.claim: A person becomes joyful, insolent, boastful, and transgressive when he sees himself as self-sufficient and his wealth has increased.
IBNKATHIR:96:6/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن الإنسان أنه ذو فرح وأشر وبطر وطغيان ، إذا رأى نفسه قد استغنى وكثر ماله

IBNKATHIR:96:7/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:7/r1.claim: A person becomes joyful, insolent, boastful, and transgressive when he sees himself as self-sufficient and his wealth has increased.
IBNKATHIR:96:7/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن الإنسان أنه ذو فرح وأشر وبطر وطغيان ، إذا رأى نفسه قد استغنى وكثر ماله

IBNKATHIR:96:8/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:8/r2.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR:96:8/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh says worldly and knowledge seekers are both insatiable but unequal: the learned gain God's approval, while the worldly person persists in transgression; he connects 96:6–7 with 35:28.
IBNKATHIR:96:8/r2.anchor: عن عون قال : قال عبد الله : مَنهومان لا يشبعان

MAWARDI:96:7/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:7/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:96:7/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas understands the person to see himself as independent of his Lord.
MAWARDI:96:7/r1.anchor: أي عن ربه ، قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI:96:7/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:7/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:7/r2.claim: The phrase may instead mean that he feels self-sufficient because of his wealth and riches.
MAWARDI:96:7/r2.anchor: ويحتمل ثانياً : استغنى بماله وثروته ، وقال الكلبي : نزلت

MAWARDI:96:7/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:7/r3.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI:96:7/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says the passage was revealed about Abu Jahl.
MAWARDI:96:7/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي : نزلت في أبي جهل .

NASAFI:96:7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:7/r1.claim: The phrase means that a person sees himself as self-sufficient; with verbs of thought, “I saw myself” means “I knew myself.”

NASAFI:96:7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:7/r2.claim: “Self-sufficient” is the second object of “saw”; if raʾā meant physical sight, the two pronouns could not both be its objects.
NASAFI:96:7/r2.anchor: ولو كانت بمعنى الإبصار لامتنع في فعلها الجمع بين الضميرين

QURTUBI:96:7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:7/r1.claim: The cause is seeing himself as self-sufficient, with wealth and abundance.
QURTUBI:96:7/r1.anchor: " أن رآه " أي لأن رأى نفسه استغنى ، أي صار ذا مال وثروة .

QURTUBI:96:7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:7/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:96:7/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, via Abu Salih, reports that Abu Jahl asked Muhammad for Meccan mountains of gold so the polytheists might become rich, transgress, and abandon their religion for his; Gabriel offered to grant it if they wished, with punishment like the Table's people if they still rejected faith, but Muhammad refrained, knowing they would not accept.
QURTUBI:96:7/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية أبي صالح عنه ، قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية وسمع بها المشركون

QURTUBI:96:7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:7/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:7/r3.claim: Another view says Abu Jahl saw himself as self-sufficient through his clan, supporters, and helpers.
QURTUBI:96:7/r3.anchor: وقيل : " أن رآه استغنى " بالعشيرة والأنصار والأعوان .

QURTUBI:96:7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:7/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:7/r4.claim: The causal lām is omitted from an raahu, as in the example that people transgress when they see their wealth.
QURTUBI:96:7/r4.anchor: وحذف اللام من قوله " أن رآه " كما يقال : إنكم لتطغون إن رأيتم غناكم .

QURTUBI:96:7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:7/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:96:7/r5.claim: Al-Farra explains that ra'a takes a subject and predicate, like verbs of supposition; Arabic can omit nafs in such constructions, as in I saw myself or thought myself leaving.
QURTUBI:96:7/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء : لم يقل : رأى نفسه ، كما قيل : قتل نفسه

QURTUBI:96:7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:7/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:96:7/r6.claim: Mujahid, Hamid, and Qunbul from Ibn Kathir read the hamza short; the others lengthen it, which al-Qurtubi prefers.
QURTUBI:96:7/r6.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد وقنبل عن ابن كثير " أن رآه استغنى " بقصر الهمزة

RAZI:96:7/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:7/r1.speaker: الأخفش
RAZI:96:7/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash parses the phrase as meaning because he saw him, with the preposition lām omitted.
RAZI:96:7/r1.anchor: قال الأخفش : لأن رآه فحذف اللام

RAZI:96:7/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:7/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:96:7/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains that the reflexive word for self is omitted: raʾā takes a subject and predicate like verbs of supposition, and Arabic drops nafs in forms such as raʾaytanī.
RAZI:96:7/r2.anchor: قال الفراء إنما قال : { أن رآه }

RAZI:96:7/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:7/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:96:7/r3.claim: One possible sense is that a person becomes independent of God through wealth, but Rāzī rejects it: Solomon remained humble and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf did not transgress despite great wealth.

RAZI:96:7/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:7/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:96:7/r4.claim: Rāzī adds that a sensible person sees greater need of God when rich, since wealth brings concern for the safety of oneself, property, and servants, while poverty concerns the self alone.
RAZI:96:7/r4.anchor: أكثر حاجة إلى الله تعالى منه حال فقره

RAZI:96:7/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:7/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:96:7/r5.claim: His preferred sense is that the person thinks wealth came from his own striving rather than God’s gift and enabling; this is foolish because effort may end in starvation and the rich will learn their wealth was not their own power.
RAZI:96:7/r5.anchor: نالت الغنى لأنها طلبته وبذلت الجهد في الطلب

RAZI:96:7/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:7/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:96:7/r6.claim: The sūra’s beginning praises knowledge and its ending censures wealth, making religion and learning attractive and worldly riches repellent.
RAZI:96:7/r6.anchor: مدح العلم وآخرها على مذمة المال
